_comment: FAO-56 Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56 parameters. Note: Verify against local FAO-56 tables and agricultural university agronomy field guides for specific cultivar adaptations.

tomato.name: Tomato
water_saving_tips: Mulch with straw or crop residue around tomato stems to retain soil moisture and reduce weeding.
Irrigate in the early morning or evening to minimise evaporative losses.
Use furrow irrigation or drip layout rather than flood basin to prevent collar rot.

wheat.name: Wheat
water_saving_tips: Prioritize irrigation at Crown Root Initiation (CRI, 21 days after sowing) - missing this cuts yield.
Delay irrigation if rain is forecast in the next 48 hours.
Irrigate during cool morning hours to avoid fungal rust development.

maize.name: Maize
water_saving_tips: Use alternate furrow irrigation for row crops to cut water use by up to 30%.
Silking and grain-filling are critical moisture stages; avoid water stress during flowering.
Mulch inter-row spaces with dry crop biomass to shade soil.

cotton.name: Cotton
water_saving_tips: Furrow irrigation in alternate rows saves 25% water without reducing boll weight.
Stop irrigation when 10% bolls are open to accelerate boll bursting and prevent fibre stain.
Irrigate early morning or evening to reduce daytime wind-drift evaporation.

sandy.name: Sandy Soil
sandy.description: Light textured, low water holding capacity, drains rapidly, needs frequent light irrigations.

loam.name: Loam / Medium Black Soil
loam.description: Balanced soil with moderate infiltration and good water retention, typical of Pune plateau.

clay.name: Clay / Deep Black Soil (Vertisol)
clay.description: Heavy soil with high moisture retention, swells when wet, cracks when dry, prone to waterlogging.
